title: Geography of Pakistan
lines: USAT geography questions ask about Pakistan's provinces and capitals, neighbours, rivers and their dams and barrages, mountain ranges and peaks, passes, deserts, glaciers and lakes. These facts are stable and appear often, so tables are the best way to learn them.
## Location and neighbours
- Pakistan lies in South Asia, with the Arabian Sea to the south.
| Direction | Neighbour | Note
| East | India | the Radcliffe Line (1947) divided Punjab and Bengal
| North-east | China | linked by the Karakoram Highway through the Khunjerab Pass
| West and north-west | Afghanistan | the Durand Line (1893)
| South-west | Iran | border in Balochistan
- The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from Tajikistan.
## Administrative units
| Unit | Capital | Remember
| Punjab | Lahore | most populous province
| Sindh | Karachi | largest city and main port
| Khyber Pakhtunkhwa | Peshawar | named NWFP until 2010
| Balochistan | Quetta | largest province by area, about 44 % of the country
| Islamabad Capital Territory | Islamabad | federal capital since the 1960s
| Gilgit-Baltistan | Gilgit | high mountains and glaciers
| Azad Jammu and Kashmir | Muzaffarabad | its own government
## Rivers
- The Indus rises in Tibet near Lake Mansarovar, flows through Gilgit-Baltistan, enters the plains and falls into the Arabian Sea near Keti Bandar in Sindh.
- Eastern tributaries: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Sutlej (and the Beas in India). They join to form the Panjnad, which meets the Indus near Mithankot.
- Western tributaries: Kabul (joins at Attock), Swat, Kurram, Gomal.
- Indus Waters Treaty (1960), arranged by the World Bank: the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) went to Pakistan; the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India.
## Dams and barrages
| Structure | River | Remember
| Tarbela Dam | Indus | one of the world's largest earth-filled dams
| Mangla Dam | Jhelum | in Azad Kashmir, near Mirpur
| Warsak Dam | Kabul | near Peshawar
| Sukkur Barrage | Indus | opened 1932; once called Lloyd Barrage
| Kotri, Guddu, Taunsa barrages | Indus | irrigation canals in Sindh and Punjab
## Mountains and peaks
| Range | Highest peak | Note
| Karakoram | K2 (8,611 m) | world's second-highest peak; Baltoro and Siachen glaciers
| Himalaya | Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) | the Killer Mountain
| Hindu Kush | Tirich Mir (7,708 m) | in Chitral
| Salt Range | Sakesar | Khewra salt mine
| Sulaiman and Kirthar ranges | — | western mountains of Balochistan and Sindh
## Passes
| Pass | Links
| Khyber | Peshawar and Afghanistan
| Bolan | Quetta with Sibi and the plains
| Khunjerab | Pakistan and China (Karakoram Highway)
| Lowari | Dir and Chitral
| Kohat, Gomal, Tochi | routes through the western hills
| Babusar | Kaghan valley and Chilas
## Climate
- Most of Pakistan is arid or semi-arid. The south and the plains have very hot summers; Jacobabad and Sibi are among the hottest places in the country.
- The summer monsoon (roughly July to September) brings most of the rain to the north-east, especially upper Punjab and Kashmir. Winter rain and snow come from western disturbances.
- The northern mountains are cold, with heavy snow, and feed the rivers through melting glaciers in summer. This is why river flows and floods peak in the hot months.
## Natural regions
- Northern mountains: Karakoram, Himalaya and Hindu Kush.
- Western mountains: Sulaiman, Kirthar and the ranges of Balochistan.
- Indus plain: the fertile, irrigated heartland of Punjab and Sindh.
- Plateaus and deserts: Potohar, Balochistan, Thar, Cholistan and Thal.
- Coastal areas: the Makran coast of Balochistan and the Indus delta with mangrove forests.
## Deserts, plateaus and lakes
- Deserts: Thar (Sindh), Cholistan (Punjab), Thal (between Indus and Jhelum), Kharan (Balochistan).
- Plateaus: Potohar (between the Indus and Jhelum) and the Balochistan plateau.
- Lakes: Manchar (largest freshwater lake, Sindh), Keenjhar or Kalri (water for Karachi), Saiful Muluk (Kaghan valley).
- Ports: Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar. Gwadar was bought from Oman in 1958.
> The Kabul River joins the Indus at  (A) Mithankot  (B) Attock  (C) Tarbela  (D) Sukkur
> B. Mithankot is where the Panjnad meets the Indus, a common mix-up.
> Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which river went to India?  (A) Jhelum  (B) Chenab  (C) Ravi  (D) Indus
> C. Remember "western to Pakistan": Indus, Jhelum, Chenab. The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej went to India.
## Traps
! Punjab is the most populous province, but Balochistan is the largest by area.
! K2 is in the Karakoram, not the Himalaya; Nanga Parbat is in the Himalaya.
! Mangla is on the Jhelum and Tarbela on the Indus. Do not swap them.
## Quick check
- Neighbours: India, China, Afghanistan, Iran.
- Capitals: Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Quetta; Gilgit; Muzaffarabad.
- K2 Karakoram; Nanga Parbat Himalaya; Tirich Mir Hindu Kush.
- Khyber–Peshawar; Bolan–Quetta; Khunjerab–China.
